<description>
`AnalyzePSBT` computes `fee = in_amt - out_amt` once every input amount is known and returns it as is. A PSBT whose outputs are worth more than its inputs therefore gets a negative `fee` and a `next` role of updater, even though no wallet can ever sign it into a valid transaction. The function already returns `PSBT is not valid. ...` for bad input values, unspendable outputs and an out-of-range output total.

An output total above the input total is reported the same way:

```
before: {"fee": -1.00000000, "next": "updater", ...}
after:  {"next": "creator", "error": "PSBT is not valid. Output amount larger than input amount"}
```

The functional test builds a PSBT that spends a 1 BTC output into a 2 BTC output and checks the error and the `creator` role. Without the change the assertion on `next` fails. `rpc_psbt.py`, `wallet_send.py`, `wallet_multisig_descriptor_psbt.py`, `rpc_openrpc.py` and the psbt unit tests pass.
</description>

<commits>
8262933013 psbt: analyzepsbt reports an error when outputs exceed inputs

When every input amount is known, AnalyzePSBT computed fee as
in_amt - out_amt and returned it even if it was negative, together with
a negative fee rate and a next role of updater or signer. Treat a PSBT
that pays out more than it spends as invalid, like the other amount
checks in the same function.
</commits>
